answer: Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 21 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. Because the yarrow solution is checked at the marble gate and logged, the mesa audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch as a result pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. That is 29 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
